findings.claim: A cancelled order can be transitioned back to paid, resurrecting an order that should be terminal and allowing downstream payment or fulfillment processing to proceed for a cancelled order.
evidence: evals/cases/case_09/src/orders.py:6 explicitly defines the transition from cancelled to paid.
evals/cases/case_09/src/orders.py:10-15 accepts every transition present in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS without any additional guard.
A direct runtime check of transition_order({"id": 9, "status": "cancelled"}, "paid") returned {"id": 9, "status": "paid"}.
evals/cases/case_09/tests/test_orders.py:4-7 only tests created to paid and does not protect the terminal behavior of cancelled orders.

uncertainties: No business specification is included in the case; the review infers from standard order lifecycle semantics and the explicit terminal delivered state that cancelled orders must not be directly resurrected as paid.
